newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X expects interim report next week.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X expects interim report next week.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Friday it expected to receive an interim report by the end of next week on the Busang audit being conducted by Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd.
"Upon receiving and reviewing the interim report, Bre-X will be promptly issuing a press release relating to the interim report," the Calgary-based gold prospector said in a statement.
Bre-X also released a copy of a status report on the Busang audit outlining how and when Strathcona would release its findings.
"At this time, we anticipate the principal conclusions to be expressed in our interim report will remain unchanged in our final report," Strathcona said in its report to Bre-X.
Strathcona said it expected to issue an interim report to Bre-X and any other parties Bre-X designated, at the end of next week.
Strathcona said the interim report would include its compilation of assay data, an interpretation of the data and other main observations of its technical audit.
A complete final report would follow in about six weeks, the statement said.
Results from assay labs in Canada and in Indonesia, along with the results from a lab in Australia, should be available in the latter part of next week, Strathcona said.

"The laboratories are aware of the sensitive nature of this data and although a number of individuals will be aware of the program being followed, only one or two persons in management at each laboratory will have access to the final assays," the statement said.
Strathcona said it instructed the laboratories not to release their results to Strathcona until they were notified that work had been completed at all locations.
"The assays will be done by both fire assay and bottle cyanide leach techniques so that six assays will be available for every two-metre interval," Strathcona said.
It said 175 samples of crushed material representing 350 metres of drill core would have been delivered to assay labs as of April 25.

The assay results from this initial group of samples were expected to be representative of the full 1,470 metres of core recovered from Strathcona's six-hole drilling program at Busang, the company said.
